intro: We hold a recorded total fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh for {{count}} published MBA / PGDM colleges in India. This list is a starting point for the best MBA colleges under ₹5 lakh, as long as you read the programme name on each card.
Ranked colleges come first among the top MBA colleges in India 2026. After them, colleges are ordered by the recorded fee, lowest first, which is why some little-known institutes appear early.
listLead: A card may show an executive diploma or a short management-development course rather than the two-year full-time MBA. If the programme name is not the degree you want, skip the fee and check the official notice.
snapshot: Among the {{feeN}} published colleges here, the median recorded total fee is {{feeMedian}}. The middle half sits between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}.

Our records place 147 of these colleges under ₹1 lakh and another 147 between ₹1 lakh and ₹3 lakh. A figure near the floor of this list is often one year of fee, or a short course, not the full two-year cost.
Most colleges here are private ({{private}}), with {{public}} public institutes. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu have the most listings.
firstCollegesLead: IIFT's recorded full-time MBA in International Business total is ₹21.82 lakh, and IIT Delhi's official full-time MBA tuition is ₹12 lakh. Both are above this cap, so neither flagship appears on this under-₹5 lakh list.
The IIT Delhi DMS admission page states that tuition for the two-year full-time MBA is ₹12 lakh, so that programme does not belong under ₹5 lakh. Confirm every low fee on the official notice.

sections.heading: Why some well-known names appear under ₹5 lakh
paragraphs: IIT Delhi, IIFT and IIT Kharagpur are 4th, 17th and 12th in the NIRF 2025 Management ranking. They appear here because the fee we hold is for a shorter course, not because the flagship MBA costs under ₹5 lakh.

compare.heading: How to shortlist the best MBA colleges under ₹5 lakh
paragraphs: A genuine two-year public MBA and a one-year executive diploma are not priced the same way. Start with the award and the duration, then look at the number.
On the official fee notice, check:
bullets: Whether the fee covers the full programme or only one year, and whether hostel, mess and exam charges are extra.
Whether the course is an MBA, a PGDM, an executive diploma or a short certificate.
The entrance test (CAT, CMAT, MAT, ATMA, TANCET or a state test) and the latest cut-off.
The latest official placement report. A low fee is only useful if the programme is the one you will actually join.

faqs.question: How many MBA colleges in India have a fee under ₹5 lakh here?
faqs.answer: {{count}} published MBA / PGDM colleges in our records have a main-programme fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh. Colleges with no fee on file, or a fee we treat as a data error, are left out.

faqs.question: What is a typical fee on this under-₹5 lakh list?
faqs.answer: The median recorded total fee is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half falls between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}. Many of the lowest figures need a second look, because they may cover only one year.

faqs.question: Is IIT Delhi's MBA really under ₹5 lakh?
faqs.answer: No. The IIT Delhi DMS admission page lists tuition of ₹12 lakh for the two-year full-time MBA, which is above this cap, so IIT Delhi is not on this list.

faqs.question: Why is IIFT on a list of colleges under ₹5 lakh?
faqs.answer: The recorded fee for IIFT's full-time MBA in International Business is now ₹21.82 lakh, which is above this cap, so IIFT is not on this list.

faqs.question: Why are some very low fees missing?
faqs.answer: We treat recorded fees under ₹10,000 as data errors and do not quote them as a minimum. That includes a JNU MBA figure of ₹359 and a few other sub-₹10,000 rows.
